name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Grijalva with large fundraising advantage
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Grijalva: a D+13 district, incumbency, and a 10-to-1 fundraising edge over Butierez, with prediction markets pricing a Democratic win around 95%. No polls or expert ratings exist, so the forecast rests on these structural advantages.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Grijalva would be the first signal of movement in this low-attention race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Adelita Grijalva, the Democratic incumbent in this heavily Democratic Tucson-area district, seeks a full term after winning the seat. The district's partisan lean of D+13 gives her a substantial structural advantage, and she has raised roughly $2.3 million with over $400,000 in cash, far outpacing Republican Daniel Butierez, who has raised about $224,000 with little cash remaining and no outside support.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near 95%. The seat is rated Safe D, with Grijalva strongly favored to hold it.
